probes.question: The endowment effect is the finding that people are more likely to do what?
options: Retain an object they own than acquire that same object

probes.question: True or false: in the Cornell mug study, owners required about the same amount to sell the mug as others were willing to pay.

image.alt: Flat illustration of a plain teal mug with steam rising from it.

body.question: Cornell University undergraduates were given a mug, then offered the chance to sell it. Compared with what participants were willing to pay to acquire the mug, how much did owners require to sell it?
body.reveal: Approximately twice as high. In this study by Daniel Kahneman, Jack Knetsch and Richard Thaler, the amount required once ownership was established ("willingness to accept") was approximately twice as high as the amount participants were willing to pay ("willingness to pay").
